  2. Assume is symmetric and positive definite, then

    (12)f(x)=xTAx+bTx+c=(Ax+b)Tx

    note that the i-th item of f(x) is (∑j=1najxj+bi)xi=aixi2+(∑j=1,j≠inajxj+bi)xi, which is maximized when xi=−∑j=1,j≠inajxj+bi2ai by the result given. Go through all i from 1 to n, we'd have n equations, and they can be written in matrix form:

    (13)∀ 1⩽i⩽n,xi=−∑j=1,j≠inajxj+bi2ai⇒2Ax+b=0n

    since is symmetric and positive definite, it is also invertible, therefore the solution to the equation, x∗=−12A−1b.

    Let x=x∗+Δx, we have

    (14)f(x∗+Δx)=(Ax∗+AΔx+b)T(x∗+Δx)=f(x∗)+ΔxT(2Ax∗+b)+ΔxTAΔx=f(x∗)+ΔxTAΔx

    Since is positive definite, for any Δx∈Rn, there will be f(x∗+Δx)⩾f(x∗), and the 'equality' hold iff. Δx=0. This implies that x∗ is indeed a global minimum point for f(x).

    Therefore we generalized the result to the following theorem:

    If is positive definite, f(x)=xTAx+bTx+c, then f(x) has a unique global minimum point x∗=−12A−1b.

    Similarly, we'd have: if is negative definite, f(x)=xTAx+bTx+c, then f(x) has a unique global maximum point x∗=−12A−1b.

Question 5

Let g(x,y)=f(λx+(1−λ)y)−λf(x)−(1−λ)f(y), since f(x)≡1−xTx, we have

(23)g(x,y)=1−(λx+(1−λ)y)T(λx+(1−λ)y)−λ(1−xTx)−(1−λ)(1−yTy)=λλ¯(xTx−2xTy+yTy)=λλ¯(x−y)T(x−y)⩾0

where λ¯=1−λ, for any λ∈(0,1), and '=' holds iff. x=y. hence ∀ x,y∈Rn,x≠y,λ∈(0,1), we have g(x,y)>0, i.e.

(24)f(λx+(1−λ)y)>λf(x)+(1−λ)f(y)

this indicates that f(x) is strictly concave.

  2. For a primal-format linear programming problem

    (32)maxxcTx,subject to.Ax⩽b,x⩾0n

    if x1,x2 are the 2 distinct solutions, x3=λx1+(1−λ)x2, λ∈(0,1), is a convex combination of x1,x2, then

    (33)cTx3=cT(λx1+(1−λ)x2)=λcTx1+(1−λ)cTx2=λM+(1−λ)M=M

    where M is the optimal value. And

    (34)Ax3=λAx1+(1−λ)Ax2⩽λb+(1−λ)b=bx3=λx1+(1−λ)x2⩾0
